newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan president calls for British "understanding".
newsitem.headline: Kenyan president calls for British "understanding".

text.p: President Daniel arap Moi opened Britain's new 10 million pound ($16 million) embassy in Kenya on Friday saying he expected the former colonial ruler to be "more understanding" than other countries.
Britain, Kenya's largest foreign investor and trading partner, seldom joins publicly in foreign criticism of official corruption and human rights abuses in the East African country.
"Britain should understand more and better than other countries" who had no colonial past in Africa, Moi said, describing the two countries as "inseparable".

The 72-year-old president referred jokingly to the last major bilateral squabble when Britain's overseas aid minister Lynda Chalker threatened in 1995 to freeze aid until she was satisfied about political and economic reforms and human rights.
Turning to Chalker, present at Friday's ceremony, Moi said: "I want you to feel at home while you are here -- no controversies."
Chalker said in her speech results of Kenya's economic liberalisation were encouraging. She said general elections in Kenya due in the next year were a vital ingredient to build democracy.
"Our greatest hope is that Kenyans will make their important choices freely, fairly and -- above all -- peacefully. This will be the best guarantee for future stability," she said.
